## Conference overview

*Preview by Adam Burke, p. 215. Reproduced in full.*


> The Mid-American Conference performed a one-for-one swap this offseason, shipping off Northern Illinois to the Mountain West and acquiring Sacramento State from the Big Sky Conference at the FCS level.

> If you don’t understand that trade from a geographic standpoint, neither do I, but the Hornets signed a five-year deal to be a football-only MAC member, as the basketball team will play in the Big West.

> With UMass rejoining the MAC last season, the conference has 13 teams, with three in Michigan, one in New York, six in Ohio, one in Indiana, one in Massachusetts, and then one in California.

> As usual, realignment remains a head-scratcher, but we sure have some fascinating travel spots for this season as a result, especially when we get to MACtion in late October and early November with weeknight games.

> On the whole, the conference isn’t very strong again, but somebody will have to win it.

> UMass went 0-12 and 0-8 in conference play at one extreme, while Western Michigan went 10-4, including a 7-1 record against MAC opponents.

> The Broncos put an exclamation point on their season with a 10-point win over Miami (OH) in Detroit for the MAC Championship and a slaughter of Kennesaw State in the Myrtle Beach Bowl.

> WMU (+360) is co-favored to run it back and their company is Miami, so we could be looking at our first MAC Championship Game rematch since Northern Illinois and Bowling Green played three straight title games from 2013-15.

> The Falcons (16-1) may not be much of a factor, but their archrival Toledo (4-1) is getting some market love, even with former head coach Jason Candle at UConn.

> Ohio (+650) and Central Michigan (+750) round out the single-digit shots in what looks like a wide-open conference again.

> Three teams tied for second at 6-2 last season and there was a battle until the end in 2024 with two teams at 7-1 and two at 6-2.

> It usually comes down to the last week to see who will represent the conference at Ford Field and this season looks to follow that same path. mac

## Quarterback themes


**From the conference preview (p. 215):**

> *Not addressed in guide.*


**From the team pages in this conference** — 13 of 13 teams' pages address this theme. A sample follows; Phase 3 carries the full treatment team by team.


- **Akron Zips** (p. 217) — Moorhead was a longtime OC and QB coach before taking on this challenging job.

- **Ball State Cardinals** (p. 219) — However, there is no clear-cut answer as to whether or not any of the guys in the QB room can be FBS-level starters, even in the MAC.

- **Bowling Green Falcons** (p. 220) — The Falcons lost four times as a favorite to MAC opponents and mustered very little on offense, especially in the passing game.

- **Buffalo Bulls** (p. 223) — Everything starts with the QB and we saw that last season, as Buffalo excelled on special teams and played well on defense, but Roberson couldn’t keep up with what Ogbonna did the year prior.

- **Central Michigan Chippewas** (p. 224) — Are you a quarterback who would rather run the ball than throw it?

- **Eastern Michigan Eagles** (p. 227) — The team’s three leading tacklers are back, the starting QB, and top WR, and that’s seemingly a rarity in the current landscape of college football.

- **Kent State Golden Flashes** (p. 229) — The Dru in question is Dru DeShields, who basically came out of nowhere last season to post an 18/3 TD/INT ratio with just over 2,000 passing yards.

- **Massachusetts Minutemen** (p. 231) — It is also Year 2 for Harasymiak and his assistants, although OC Mike Bajakian won’t be along for the ride, as he’s the new QB coach of the Cleveland Browns (I swear, the jokes write themselves with that organization).

**From the conference preview (p. 215):**

> WMU (+360) is co-favored to run it back and their company is Miami, so we could be looking at our first MAC Championship Game rematch since Northern Illinois and Bowling Green played three straight title games from 2013-15.

**From the team pages in this conference** — 13 of 13 teams' pages address this theme. A sample follows; Phase 3 carries the full treatment team by team.


- **Akron Zips** (p. 216) — The Zips failed to win more games than they lost for the 10th consecutive season, as a 7-7 showing in 2017 is the best outcome for the program since going 8-5 under Terry Bowden back in 2015.

- **Ball State Cardinals** (p. 218) — Returning production would have been an oxymoron here, but Ball State has next to none of it anyway, so Uremovich starts Year 2 with essentially a brand-new roster.

- **Bowling Green Falcons** (p. 221) — Austyn Dendy looks like the feature back and had a solid freshman season with 4.6 yards per carry, but his 108 carries barely outpaced Chris McMillian with 84 and Cameron Pettaway with 72.

- **Buffalo Bulls** (p. 222) — Lembo gets a lot out of his talent and I think his program bounces back.

- **Central Michigan Chippewas** (p. 225) — With a lot of returning linemen and some transfer portal acquisitions, Central Michigan is going to play a run-heavy, ball-control style of offense.

- **Eastern Michigan Eagles** (p. 227) — Championship steve makinen power rating make the playoff RANK # CONFERENCE: NATIONAL: # RANK Is this a case study in returning production in the transfer portal era?

- **Kent State Golden Flashes** (p. 229) — Here’s the thing - DeShields staying healthy is vital because there is absolutely no FBS experience behind him.

- **Massachusetts Minutemen** (p. 230) — Now it’s UMass who hasn’t beaten a FBS team in a while, as their last win was against Army back on October 8, 2023, a game in which Kay’Ron Lynch-Adams ran for 234 yards.

## Transfer-portal themes


**From the conference preview (p. 215):**

> *Not addressed in guide.*


**From the team pages in this conference** — 13 of 13 teams' pages address this theme. A sample follows; Phase 3 carries the full treatment team by team.


- **Akron Zips** (p. 216) — There is no bowl ban for this season and it seems like the program got a little bit more investment than usual, as the school in the heart of the Rubber City has among the lowest NIL budgets in FBS.

- **Ball State Cardinals** (p. 219) — Mountain Lions after transferring out of Wake Forest.

- **Bowling Green Falcons** (p. 220) — We’ll never know if things would have gone better had Notre Dame/Missouri transfer Drew Pyne not gotten hurt, as four different quarterbacks saw action and they collectively had as many touchdowns (12) as interceptions.

- **Buffalo Bulls** (p. 223) — With a very light NIL budget, I’m guessing they invested pretty heavily in this kid.

- **Central Michigan Chippewas** (p. 225) — With a lot of returning linemen and some transfer portal acquisitions, Central Michigan is going to play a run-heavy, ball-control style of offense.

- **Eastern Michigan Eagles** (p. 226) — The program heads into 2026 with the lowest-ranked transfer portal class in the conference per 247Sports, but also tied with in-state rival Central Michigan for the largest freshman class.

- **Kent State Golden Flashes** (p. 229) — There is a fascinating dynamic on Cherokee Valeria’s defense, as there are portal players that are seniors and some homegrown talent that will play big roles as sophomores.

- **Massachusetts Minutemen** (p. 231) — There are quite a few P4 transfers on the roster now between this portal cycle and the coaching staff’s first one.

## Schedule themes


**From the conference preview (p. 215):**

> As usual, realignment remains a head-scratcher, but we sure have some fascinating travel spots for this season as a result, especially when we get to MACtion in late October and early November with weeknight games.
>
> — *conference preview, p. 215*

> UMass went 0-12 and 0-8 in conference play at one extreme, while Western Michigan went 10-4, including a 7-1 record against MAC opponents.
>
> — *conference preview, p. 215*


**From the team pages in this conference** — 11 of 13 teams' pages address this theme. A sample follows; Phase 3 carries the full treatment team by team.


- **Akron Zips** (p. 216) — Moorhead got a lot out of a team that couldn’t make a bowl game and the most impressive data point to me was a 19-16 road win at Bowling Green after losing to rival Kent State in OT.

- **Ball State Cardinals** (p. 218) — Unfortunately for the Cardinals, two of their three most winnable conference games are road visits to Kent State and UMass.

- **Bowling Green Falcons** (p. 220) — The Falcons play Nebraska, Iowa State, and South Florida in non-conference, so that’ll be a tough stretch, plus conference play starts with perennial contender Miami of Ohio on the road.

- **Buffalo Bulls** (p. 222) — However, the schedule is pretty kind with two FCS opponents at home in non-conference, plus home games against UMass and Bowling Green.

- **Central Michigan Chippewas** (p. 224) — The conference schedule is a bit tougher for the Chips, but they host Sac State and only play three true conference road games, with one against lowly Ball State.

- **Eastern Michigan Eagles** (p. 226) — With a neutral-site game against Central Michigan, the Eagles only play three conference home games.

- **Kent State Golden Flashes** (p. 228) — It will be a challenge to match the five wins from last season, given that the Flashes play Sacramento State on the road on a short week after the rivalry game against Akron and don’t have the luxury of seeing UMass on the schedule.

- **Massachusetts Minutemen** (p. 230) — This was a truly terrible team that got outgained at home by Bryant and lost all eight conference games by an average score of 38-11.

## Historical and situational notes


**From the conference preview (p. 215):**

> With UMass rejoining the MAC last season, the conference has 13 teams, with three in Michigan, one in New York, six in Ohio, one in Indiana, one in Massachusetts, and then one in California.
>
> — *conference preview, p. 215*

> WMU (+360) is co-favored to run it back and their company is Miami, so we could be looking at our first MAC Championship Game rematch since Northern Illinois and Bowling Green played three straight title games from 2013-15.
>
> — *conference preview, p. 215*

> Three teams tied for second at 6-2 last season and there was a battle until the end in 2024 with two teams at 7-1 and two at 6-2.
>
> — *conference preview, p. 215*


**From the team pages in this conference** — 13 of 13 teams' pages address this theme. A sample follows; Phase 3 carries the full treatment team by team.


- **Akron Zips** (p. 216) — The Zips failed to win more games than they lost for the 10th consecutive season, as a 7-7 showing in 2017 is the best outcome for the program since going 8-5 under Terry Bowden back in 2015.

- **Ball State Cardinals** (p. 218) — Last year’s dismal offensive performance with just 15.8 PPG led to the fourth straight season without a bowl game and Ball State hasn’t had a winning record in conference play outside of the 2020 COVID season since 2013.

- **Bowling Green Falcons** (p. 220) — I felt like the Falcons were one of the more interesting teams that I wrote up last season because they hired former Ohio State standout and Tennessee State miracle worker Eddie George as the head coach.

- **Buffalo Bulls** (p. 222) — But, this past season, Buffalo went 5-7 and even the wins were scary, beating Kent State by only a field goal as a 23.5-point favorite and then barely beating Eastern Michigan and UMass as substantial favorites.

- **Central Michigan Chippewas** (p. 225) — Drinkall is looking to run a lot of 21 personnel, as he has a mobile QB in Angel Flores, who was the team’s secondleading rusher and top touchdown-getter last season.

- **Eastern Michigan Eagles** (p. 226) — However, after records of 5-7 and 4-8, the Eagles have missed the bowl season in consecutive years for the first time since 2014-15, Creighton’s first two years with the team.

- **Kent State Golden Flashes** (p. 228) — It will be a challenge to match the five wins from last season, given that the Flashes play Sacramento State on the road on a short week after the rivalry game against Akron and don’t have the luxury of seeing UMass on the schedule.

- **Massachusetts Minutemen** (p. 230) — The Minutemen really put the “ass” in UMass last season, as they were 0-12 and scored just 11.1 PPG.
